We completely switched our project to dayjs and at the end noticed that dayjs does not support the daylight saving time. I can only warn against using this library. Operations such as add cause unexpected results. As soon as a calculation goes over the limit of the time change, the result is wrong. We will continue to use moment.js. dayjs('25-10-2020', 'DD-MM-YYYY')
          .tz('Europe/Berlin')
          .add(1, 'day')
          .diff(dayjs('26-10-2020', 'DD-MM-YYYY').tz('Europe/Berlin'), 'days')
          .toString()
          

result = -3600000

FYI, I have created a dayjs plugin to solve this issue.
https://www.npmjs.com/package/dayjs-timezone-iana-plugin 

The code is quite simple and largely inspired by moment-timezone.
It includes the complete and latest IANA databases 2021e (96KB compressed).  It takes more space than the method used by DayJS or Luxon. But it works even if NodeJS is compiled with small-icu.

We will update it regularly and we used it already in production.

```js
const date1 = dayjs('2020-10-24').tz('Europe/London').add(2, 'day').toISOString();

```

issues.title: Timezone startOf DST off-by-one
issues.body:
In Australia DST ends on the 4th of April 2021.

Using the timezone plugin and v1.10.4 (latest):

- Getting the start of the day before this date (in DST) returns the correct value
- Getting the start of the day after this date (outside DST) returns an incorrect value.

```js
dayjs.tz('2021-04-01 08:00', 'Australia/Melbourne').startOf('day').format()
// 2021-04-01T00:00:00+11:00 (correct)

dayjs.tz('2021-04-15 08:00', 'Australia/Melbourne').startOf('day').format()
// 2021-04-14T23:00:00+11:00 (incorrect)
```

Curiously, the changelog mentions this issue was fixed in v1.9.7, so I switched to 1.9.6 to test this and it seems to be working correctly:

```js
dayjs.tz('2021-04-01 08:00', 'Australia/Melbourne').startOf('day').format()
// 2021-04-01T00:00:00+11:00 (correct)

dayjs.tz('2021-04-15 08:00', 'Australia/Melbourne').startOf('day').format()
// 2021-04-15T00:00:00+11:00 (correct)
```

Is anyone up for fixing this? I'll throw a $100 bounty down. Surely there are some others who also need this fixed and want to add to the pool!

This is using April 1st to show what the date looks like. Offset and local offset are correct at +11. Date itself appears correct too.

## Finding 2

Now doing this at April 15th. Everything still is correct. Offset is +10.

```
> dayjs.tz('2021-04-15 08:00', 'Australia/Melbourne');

  '$L': 'en',
  '$d': 2021-04-14T22:00:00.000Z,
```

## Finding 3

Here I did `startOf` for April 15th and the problem was introduced. There was a change a few releases back regarding `startOf`,`endOf`, and I wonder if that's when this bug was introduced.

Here's what I notice that's wrong:
* No `$localOffset` in `$x`

During a daylight saving change, there will be an hour missing in the browser timezone.
Say the browser goes from utc+1 to utc+2 on a given day,

will print `03:00` in Central European Summer Time (UTC+2) because `02:00` doesn't exists.
If you try to change timezone to a timezone that doesn't have daylight saving change (let's say utc+3)

This is because dayjs always use the local as a reference

the time should exist and et right

comments.author: caork

comments.body:
This also breaks plain conversions, not only setting a time. On dayjs 1.11.23 with the system zone in America/Vancouver (same results in Chrome, Firefox, Safari and Bun; all correct with the system zone in UTC):

```js
dayjs('2025-03-09T06:30:00Z').tz('America/Havana').toISOString()
// 2025-03-09T07:30:00.000Z: a different instant (02:30 in Havana doesn't exist in Vancouver that day)

dayjs('2025-03-09T06:30:00Z').utcOffset(-240).format()
// 2025-03-09T03:30:00-04:00: right instant, wrong hour (expected 02:30)
```

Both come from storing the zoned date as a local `Date` shifted by the offset (`proto.tz` parses `toLocaleString` output locally, and `utcOffset` reads local getters), so any shifted time in the system zone's DST gap moves by an hour.

issues.title: +00:00 timezone bug
issues.body:
This line is causing several bugs when working with +00:00 timezones (for example Europe/Lisbon):
https://github.com/iamkun/dayjs/blob/b5a1391011b247d08863d291542db5937b23b427/src/plugin/utc/index.js#L117
It is because $localOffset is 0 (this is correct offset) and therefore value of `(new Date()).getTimezoneOffset()` is used (instead of the value 0). 
Operator || cannot be used here, because it does not work correctly with $localOffset == 0.
This line should be changed into:
```
? this.$offset + (this.$x.$localOffset === null || this.$x.$localOffset === undefined ? (new Date()).getTimezoneOffset()) : 0
```

comments.author: DimaBur

comments.body:
Confirmed this still reproduces in **Day.js 1.11.23** (current npm latest), as well as **1.11.13**, through the public `dayjs.tz(string, zone)` API. Here is a minimal reproduction with no mocks or application code.

### Reproduction

```sh
mkdir dayjs-zero-offset-repro
cd dayjs-zero-offset-repro
npm init -y
npm install dayjs@1.11.23
```

Save as `repro.cjs`:

```js
const dayjs = require('dayjs');
dayjs.extend(require('dayjs/plugin/utc'));
dayjs.extend(require('dayjs/plugin/timezone'));

console.log(dayjs.tz('2026-10-24 19:30', 'America/Los_Angeles').toISOString());
console.log(dayjs.tz('2026-03-29 09:30', 'Asia/Tokyo').toISOString());
```

Run in separate processes:

```sh
TZ=Europe/London node repro.cjs
TZ=UTC node repro.cjs
```

Expected in **both** environments:

```text
2026-10-25T02:30:00.000Z
2026-03-29T00:30:00.000Z
```

Actual with `TZ=Europe/London`:

```text
2026-10-25T03:30:00.000Z
2026-03-29T01:30:00.000Z
```

`TZ=UTC` gives the expected results. Both target wall-clock times are unambiguous: this is not a gap/overlap in the explicitly selected target timezone. The result incorrectly depends on the host timezone.

### Diagnosis

Tracing the first example in 1.11.13, the timezone plugin initially computes the correct instant `2026-10-25T02:30:00.000Z`, then calls `d(targetTs).utcOffset(targetOffset)`.

At that point:

- `targetOffset` is `-420`.
- The stored `$x.$localOffset` is `0`: London has already returned to GMT at the target instant.
- The intermediate `$d` represents `2026-10-24T19:30:00.000Z`, when London was still on daylight saving time; `$d.getTimezoneOffset()` is `-60`.
- In `valueOf()`, `$x.$localOffset || $d.getTimezoneOffset()` discards the valid `0` and uses `-60`, shifting the resulting timestamp by one hour.

Source references: [timezone factory](https://github.com/iamkun/dayjs/blob/v1.11.13/src/plugin/timezone/index.js#L132-L135), [utcOffset](https://github.com/iamkun/dayjs/blob/v1.11.13/src/plugin/utc/index.js#L90-L95), [valueOf](https://github.com/iamkun/dayjs/blob/v1.11.13/src/plugin/utc/index.js#L108-L111).

Using nullish selection instead of `||` in a standalone diagnostic calculation restores the expected timestamp for this case. This is **not** a claim that changing that expression alone fully fixes formatting or all related behavior; those paths need separate regression coverage.

### Tested scope

On 1.11.13, both cases above are one hour late with host zones `Europe/London`, `Europe/Dublin`, `Europe/Lisbon`, and `Atlantic/Canary`. The same cases are correct with `UTC`, `Atlantic/Reykjavik`, `Europe/Berlin`, `America/Los_Angeles`, and `Asia/Shanghai`. An ordinary-date control case is correct. Both the London and UTC cases were also rerun on 1.11.23 with the results shown above.

Environment: Node.js v24.18.0, macOS 27.0.1, using the `TZ` environment variable per process. No browser reproduction or other Day.js versions are claimed here.

issues.title: fix localized format for `cs` locale
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**
Localized formats for the `cs` locale use the nominative month name when a day comes before the month. In Czech the month after a day is in the genitive. The locale only has the nominative names (`leden_únor_…_říjen_…`), so `LL`, `LLL` and `LLLL` (and any format like `D. MMMM YYYY`) are wrong.

Take a look at the [moment implementation](https://github.com/moment/moment/blob/develop/locale/cs.js), which has separate `standalone` and `format` month lists.

```js
import dayjs from 'dayjs'
import localizedFormat from 'dayjs/plugin/localizedFormat'
import 'dayjs/locale/cs'

dayjs.extend(localizedFormat)
dayjs('2026-10-16').locale('cs').format('LL') // "16. říjen 2026"
```

**Expected behavior**
For `October 16 2026`:
- `LL`: `16. října 2026` (not `16. říjen 2026`)
- `LLL`: `16. října 2026 13:30`
- `LLLL`: `pátek 16. října 2026 13:30`

A month on its own (`MMMM`) stays in the nominative: `říjen`.

Genitive names: `ledna_února_března_dubna_května_června_července_srpna_září_října_listopadu_prosince`

**Information**
 - Day.js Version v1.11.23

issues.title: diff(..., 'year'|'month', true) returns 0 instead of NaN for an Invalid Date operand
issues.author: yfwmaniish

comments.body:
Confirmed on 1.11.23, and your read of `monthDiff` is right. `invalid.diff(now, 'month'|'year', true)` returns `0`, while `'day'`/`'hour'` return `NaN` because those go through the raw millisecond path and never hit `monthDiff`.

The `|| 0` at the end is doing double duty. Its real job is to turn a `-0` into `0` (a same-month, same-day diff lands on `-0` otherwise), but since `NaN` is also falsy, `NaN || 0` becomes `0` and the invalidity is lost.

The narrowest fix that keeps the `-0` cleanup and stops swallowing `NaN` is to add zero instead of or-ing it:

```js
// src/utils.js, last line of monthDiff
return -(wholeMonthDiff + ((b - anchor) / (c ? (anchor - anchor2) : (anchor2 - anchor)))) + 0
```

`x + 0` normalizes `-0` to `+0` exactly like `|| 0` did (`-0 + 0` is `+0`), but `NaN + 0` stays `NaN`. Checked it against the `Number.isNaN(x) ? NaN : +(x || 0)` form for `NaN`, `-0`, `0`, `3.5`, `-2` and they agree on every one.

Patched `dayjs.min.js` locally with that single change and ran it end to end:

```
invalid.diff(a, 'month', true)   NaN            (was 0)
invalid.diff(a, 'year',  true)   NaN            (was 0)
a.diff(b, 'month', true)         15.178306...   (unchanged, valid)
a.diff(sameMonth, 'month', true) 0              Object.is(-0) === false, still normalized
a.diff(b, 'day', true)           463            (ms path, untouched)
```

So `'month'`/`'year'` now propagate the Invalid Date like every other unit, and nothing else moves.
comments.author: nyxxbit

issues.title: Built `locale/ku.js` exports a wrapper object, not the locale
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**
Since #1848, `src/locale/ku.js` has a named export (`englishToArabicNumbersMap`) next to `export default locale`. Because of this, the built `locale/ku.js` sets `exports.default`, `exports.englishToArabicNumbersMap` and `__esModule`. All other locales set `module.exports = locale`.

Thus consumers get a wrapper object, not the locale:

```js
require('dayjs/locale/ku').name // undefined
Object.keys(require('dayjs/locale/ku')) // ['default', 'englishToArabicNumbersMap']
```

```js
// Node ESM
import ku from 'dayjs/locale/ku.js'
ku.name // undefined
```

Vite 8 (Rolldown) also gives the wrapper in a `"type": "module"` app. Then `dayjs.locale(ku)` has no effect, and the app stays in the previous locale. Vite 7 (Rollup) follows `__esModule` and hides the problem.

**Expected behavior**
`require('dayjs/locale/ku')` and a default ESM import give the locale object (`name === 'ku'`), the same as all other locales.

**Proposed fix**
Do not export `englishToArabicNumbersMap`. Keep it as a module-local const.

Trade-off: CJS code that reads `require('dayjs/locale/ku').default`, or that imports `englishToArabicNumbersMap`, must change. The fix restores the shape that `ku` had before #1848, and matches all other locales.

I will open a PR with the fix.
